scenario: Media-plurality researchers study only community radio stations that retained their broadcast licence. Mean weekly broadcast hours among studied stations is 5.8 (σ=1.1); the licence-retention threshold is 3.8 hours/week. The true mean broadcast hours across all stations at launch is sought.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

values.note: Only units above the survival threshold appear in the observed sample

question: (a) Assuming weekly broadcast hours is normally distributed with σ=1.1 hours/week in the full pre-filter cohort, solve numerically for the true pre-filter population mean μ such that E[X | X > 3.8] = 5.8. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much (in hours/week) does the survivor mean overstate μ? (d) What policy or scientific conclusion error arises from ignoring the survival filter?

ground_truth.explanation: The community radio stations in media-plurality academic studies dataset is a truncated-normal sample above the survival threshold t=3.8 hours/week. Solving E[X|X>t]=μ+σφ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=5.8 numerically gives μ=5.6963 hours/week. Only 95.76% of the original cohort survived; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 0.1037 hours/week. Ignoring the filter leads to over-estimating the baseline quality/capacity of the full cohort, producing over-optimistic policy conclusions.

naive_answer: The true mean weekly broadcast hours is 5.8 hours/week because that is the average observed among the surviving/studied units.
naive_trap: The observed sample consists only of units above the survival threshold. The observed mean is E[X|X>3.8] — a truncated conditional expectation — not the population mean. It systematically overstates μ whenever the threshold is non-trivially binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter ≡ truncated-normal sampling with lower truncation at t=3.8. (2) E[X|X>t] = μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ) / Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 5.8. (3) Solve numerically via brentq on [-23.7, 5.7999] → μ=5.6963. (4) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((3.8−5.6963)/1.1) = 0.95764. (5) Overstatement: 5.8−5.6963 = 0.1037 hours/week.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 5.8,1.1,3.8
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-5.6963)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.95764)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-0.1037)<0.01
